lesson_title: From Flat Card to Crisp Box
hook_text: Four steps turn a drawing into a box that stands square. Skip one and it leans for ever.
clip_script: You have the development. Now make it. Step one: mark out. Trace a template or measure every line onto the card, long folds along the grain, because card folds along its grain and cracks across it. Step two: cut. Only the outside edge and the slots. Steel ruler, cutting mat, light passes, hand well back. Never, ever cut a fold line. Step three: score and fold. Press a blunt tool, the back of a butter knife, hard along every fold line while the blank is flat. That crushes the fibres so the fold is crisp instead of a cracked bow. Bend each fold once to set it. Wrap the sides into a tube, tab inside, hold it square, glue the tab with a thin even smear, hold it a minute. Then the base. Lid last. Glue the base first and the lean is locked in for good. Step four: test. Product in. Shake, drop, stack. Diagonals equal? Lid tucks? Four steps. Square box.
visual_style: Whiteboard card sheet gets a traced development, the knife follows the dark edge only, a butter knife presses the dashed lines, the tube wraps and squares, base closes, a cupcake goes in.
pacing: Four steps at about fourteen seconds each, one warning line in each.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and score a scrap of card on both sides to see which way it folds cleanly.
